reason: This passage from 2 Samuel 13-19 demonstrates numerous instances of people freely expressing their views and opinions to authority figures, including the king. The wise woman of Tekoa openly argues her case before David, making persuasive arguments and even challenging his reasoning. Joab directly confronts King David about his behavior toward his troops. David's servants and military officers counsel him regarding battle strategy and his participation in combat. Absalom receives and considers advice from multiple counselors. Messengers report freely, and even Shimei publicly curses David. Throughout the narrative, people at various social levels voice their opinions, concerns, and counsel without evident discouragement, suggesting an active culture of dialogue and expression rather than suppression of views.
